core.title: Ashfield Allotment Society autumn green manure order
core.setting: The treasurer at Ashfield Allotment Society whose assistant tracks plot rents, waiting lists, and seed-order invoices

events.text: Standing rule from the committee: any seed, equipment or supplies order above £120 in total needs my written sign-off as chair before it is confirmed with the supplier.
Our current trade price list for societies: green manure soil-improver mix £4.20 per kilo in 5 kilo bags, pea and bean seed packets from £2.10.
Rent roll confirmed at the June meeting: 42 plots let, full plots at £32 a year and half plots at £16.
Standing rule: offers of plots to waiting-list households go strictly in list order, and each household has 14 days to reply before the offer passes to the next name.
The waiting list stands at 14 households; first on the list is Harriet Vale.
Offered the vacant half plot 17B to Harriet Vale, first on the waiting list, at the half-plot rent of £16, with 14 days to reply.
Happy to take plot 17B — please put me down for the autumn rent.
Quotation: Casablanca seed potatoes at £0.42 per kilo, minimum 200 kilos, delivered free to one address.
Ordered 200 kilos of Casablanca seed potatoes from Marshfield Tubers at £0.42 a kilo, £84 in total, well under the £120 sign-off limit, for delivery to the Trading Hut.
Catalogue note: pea 'Meteor' packets are £2.40 each and broad bean 'Aquadulce' £2.10 each this season.
Booked the Marshfield seed potato delivery for Saturday 10 October 2026 at 09:00 at the Trading Hut.
The Trading Hut opens to members on Sunday mornings, 10:00 to 12:00, through the autumn.
Decided at committee: rent invoices go out on 1 October and are due by 31 October, at the confirmed rates of £32 for full plots and £16 for half plots.
Bamboo canes, six foot, £1.10 each for orders of 50 or more.
Ordered 90 six-foot bamboo canes from Greenhaven Seeds at £1.10 each, £99 all in, under the £120 chair sign-off limit, delivered to the Trading Hut.
Quick reminder from the summer catalogue: pea 'Meteor' packets still £2.40 and broad bean 'Aquadulce' £2.10 for autumn orders.
Confirmed the autumn Trading Hut rota: Sunday openings 10:00 to 12:00 with Dev Raman as volunteer lead.
Standing rule: changes to the confirmed Trading Hut opening times need the volunteer lead's agreement first.
Order confirmation: 12 packets of pea 'Meteor' at £2.40 each, posted to Ashfield Allotment Society, total £28.80.
The waiting list is now 11 households; next in line is Owen Pratt.
Offered the half plot 22B to Owen Pratt, top of the waiting list, at the half-plot rent of £16, with 14 days to reply.
Invoice for the seed potato order: 200 kilos of Casablanca at £0.42, £84 in total, due end of October.
Apologies — a misprint crept into our catalogue: pea 'Meteor' packets are £2.60 this season, not £2.40. The broad bean price of £2.10 is correct as printed.
Introductory offer for allotment societies: green manure soil-improver mix at £3.60 per kilo this autumn, while stocks last.
The compost supplier wants our spring order numbers by November — I'll deal with that later.
Scheduled the seed potato sale day for members on Saturday 17 October 2026 at the Trading Hut, the weekend after the Marshfield delivery.
Rota is going well — three of us on most Sundays, and the Sunday morning opening hours suit everyone.
Our October delivery round to the Trading Hut is Sunday the 11th, second Sunday of the month as usual.
Reminder to members: rent invoices are due by 31 October.
To do: pay the Marshfield invoice of £84 by 31 October 2026.
Plot 17B is coming along nicely, thanks for sorting the offer so quickly.
I've accepted plot 22B and I'm starting this weekend.
The green manure soil-improver mix from Greenhaven worked well on my plot last year, by the way.
